title: Review: full project review loop 6
notes:
Maintainer risk (peer+kithd): MEDIUM — the codebase is well-structured and the auth/identity model is correct and fail-closed, but three P0 bugs (infinite retry loop on outbox receipt with missing read_at_unix, incorrect Content-Length header for peer-fetched blobs using attacker-controlled metadata, non-atomic DeliverHandler steps that can store orphan data on partial failure) must be fixed before merge; without fixes, a peer with a missing read_at field will loop forever and any peer can cause the download endpoint to advertise an incorrect Content-Length.
Confidence (peer+kithd): 80% chance no additional P0 bugs remain. Uncertainty: (1) kith-store crate was not in scope — store-layer bugs could surface at any JMAP boundary; (2) kith-chat and kith-jmap were not read — dispatcher role enforcement completeness (all owner methods really gated?) was only spot-checked via e2e tests, not by reading each handler; (3) group-chat delivery to multiple peers under concurrent outbox ticks was not exercised — the composite PK test covers enqueueing but not concurrent tick races. Would raise to 90% if: kith-chat and kith-jmap handlers were read and confirmed to gate on Role::Owner, and the store mutex hold pattern were confirmed to be identical across all handlers (no handler accidentally holds the lock across an await).
Maintainer risk (core+store): MEDIUM. kith-core clean. kith-store has V18 chat backfill bug (KITH-hqrw.40), V16 FK PRAGMA risk, 3 standalone advance_state without overflow guard. Migration complexity is primary burden.
Confidence (core+store): 85% chance of no missed P0 bug. Uncertainty: finish_message_delivery counter subquery ordering in outbox.rs, non-idempotent enqueue() failure path, V16 PRAGMA FK inside transaction. Would raise to 92% with integration tests for V18 on populated DB and enqueue duplicate path.
Maintainer risk (ctl+tui): HIGH — P0s: terminal dirty on startup failure, SSE dispatch test/code divergence, unbounded SSE buffer. P1s: indefinite reconnect on auth failure, TUI freezes from no request timeouts, incomplete ANSI stripping, dual SSE parsers drift risk, notification storm on watch restart. Dual parsers are the top long-term risk.
Confidence (ctl+tui): 85% chance of no additional P0 bugs missed. Uncertainty: (1) could not fully verify that run_sse's bytes_stream loop handles partial chunks correctly — the \r\n normalization is done per-chunk before appending, so a CRLF split across two chunks would not be normalized; (2) UI rendering correctness for non-ASCII sender names was not exercised end-to-end; (3) the interaction between scroll_offset state and terminal resize events in rapid succession. Would raise to 92% if: (a) a test for partial-chunk CRLF normalization in run_sse were added; (b) the scroll height formula in page_height() were verified to match draw_messages inner panel computation.
Maintainer risk (jmap+infra): MEDIUM — three distinct areas: (1) kith-jmap has a real is_read_only=false-for-peers protocol conformance bug and a latent error_status/notFound category mismatch; (2) kith-events LEI replay logic has a documented but understated correctness gap — the single-counter approach will silently miss replays whenever two types share a state counter value, which is routine; (3) kith-tslocal is the most solid crate in scope, with appropriate defensive boundaries and good test coverage.
Confidence (jmap+infra): 85% chance of no missed P0 bug. Uncertainty: (1) the events handler in kithd/src/events.rs is in-scope adjacent (it wires kith-events); I reviewed it fully but it is in kithd not the assigned crates; (2) the kith-store migrations were reviewed only via grep patterns, not full file read — the migration runner idempotency logic (PRAGMA user_version gating) was spot-checked not exhaustively read; (3) cargo audit was blocked by lock contention — no advisory scan completed. Would raise: any use of Argument<serde_json::Value> in actual handlers; any handler registered to the wrong map in kithd's build_dispatcher.
